name: Arch Capital Group

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Arch Capital Group logo.svg)

description: Arch is a Bermuda-based specialty insurer, reinsurer and mortgage insurer. The Insurance segment writes specialty commercial lines (property, casualty, professional liability, programs, construction, travel) in North America and London; the Reinsurance segment sells reinsurance to other insurers (property catastrophe, casualty, specialty); and the Mortgage segment insures lenders against borrower default in the U.S., Australia and Europe and offers credit-risk-transfer reinsurance to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. Profit is underwriting income plus investment income on its $47 billion of investable assets; mortgage earns over $1 billion a year on only 6 percent of premiums with a combined ratio in the teens. It is an equity-method owner of about 30 percent of French credit insurer Coface and of Somers (Greysbridge), and pays no common dividend that could be found in the pages read.

businessLines.name: Insurance
businessLines.how: Commercial specialty insurance and some reinsurance of insurance pools sold through brokers and MGAs for annual premiums; North America 73 percent of premiums, international (London market, Europe, Bermuda) 27 percent. Largest lines: property and short-tail specialty 17 percent, other liability (occurrence 17 percent, claims-made 10 percent).

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31), underwriting income (before investment income)

businessLines.name: Reinsurance
businessLines.how: Insurers and reinsurers pay premiums to lay off property catastrophe, other property, casualty, specialty, marine and aviation risk; profit swings with catastrophe losses. Premiums by line: specialty 33.4 percent, property excluding catastrophe 26.8, casualty 19.8, property catastrophe 14.1, marine and aviation 4.0.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31), underwriting income (before investment income)

businessLines.name: Mortgage
businessLines.how: Lenders and investors (and GSEs via credit-risk-transfer deals) pay premiums, mostly monthly or single, to be covered if a borrower defaults; losses are low in a stable housing market, so the combined ratio is 14.6 percent; fourth consecutive year above $1 billion of underwriting income. U.S. primary persistency 81.8 percent.

operatingProfit.period: FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31), underwriting income (before investment income)

brands.name: Coface SA (29.9 percent equity interest)
brands.note: French credit insurer; carrying value $664M at 2026-06-30 ($707M at 2025-12-31); equity-method, not consolidated

brands.name: Somers Group Holdings / Greysbridge Holdings (equity-method affiliate)
brands.note: Somers is wholly owned by Greysbridge; Arch's H1 2026 net premiums written were reduced by $308M by reinsurance deals with Somers (H1 2025: $419M)

brands.name: U.S. MidCorp and Entertainment business (acquired from Allianz, closed 2024-08-01)
brands.note: written by Fireman's Fund Insurance Company entities; premiums not separately reported in pages read
